title: Your Phone Isn’t a Tiny Gasoline Tank

segments.text: Your phone isn’t a tiny gasoline tank.
A lithium‑ion cell stores energy chemically via reversible intercalation of lithium ions, not by burning anything.
When you charge, electrical energy becomes chemical potential as lithium ions slip into the electrode material like guests finding seats.
Electrons are pushed into the negative side while lithium ions move back to their original position.
That stored chemical energy later releases as electricity when you use the device.
The electrolyte provides a conductive medium for lithium ions but does not take part in the electrochemical reaction.
So the battery stores power without ever becoming a tank.
